A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original model fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, and ablations. Appendix A.2 supplies the full instruction-following results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix A.2, including benchmark comparisons and ablation outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same reward-conditioned pair relabeling, direct preference optimization, and highest-reward inference procedure. The implicit-reward, RA+, and multi-attribute variants in Section 6.2 are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback and the same on-policy response setting. Evaluation retains AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, Arena-Hard-Auto, GSM8K, GPQA, MUSR, TruthfulQA, BBH, and ARC Challenge.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. Table 9 retains all nine baselines; Table 10 retains SimPO and OpenChat; Figure 4 retains DPA and SteerLM; the original-data DPO and additional RPO comparisons also remain.

E3.justification: The benchmark metrics, zero-shot/few-shot/CoT settings, model configurations, and training settings remain unchanged. The on-policy experiment still uses 19.8k prompts with five generated responses per prompt.

E4.justification: Section 6.2 retains the same data-reuse, implicit-reward, half-data, unlearning, inference-goal, and feedback-quality analyses. Shortening Table 5's caption does not remove its experiment or supporting evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without reported repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or removed.

E6.justification: The empirical entries in Tables 3-12 and plotted results in Figures 2-4 are unchanged. For example, Table 10 reports the same 56.57 length-controlled win rate and 52.19 win rate for the proposed method.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, DPO objective, goal-conditioned reward, and Equation (4.1) remain unchanged. Table 1 drops two illustrative conditional-policy rows, but the underlying example and reward-conditioning argument remain in Section 3.2; no mathematical reasoning is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reward augmentation, mitigating unlearning, benchmark improvements, and state-of-the-art performance with on-policy data.

C2.justification: The explanations of unlearning, reward sparsity, feedback quality, and compatibility with binarized preference data remain unchanged. Explanations shortened out of the Table 1 and Table 5 captions are retained in the body text.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 retains identical prompt templates, reward normalization, optimizer, and hyperparameters; code-access information is unchanged. Adding ArmoRM to Table 10's caption repeats the reward source already documented in Section 6.2.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and related-work positioning in Section 5 are unchanged, including distinctions from SteerLM, DPA, Conditioned-RLFT, and RPO.

P1.justification: The author list shrinks from nine authors to three, and the ByteDance affiliation is removed. Several captions are shortened or clarified, while section order and substantive body prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 removes the conditional-policy rows for rewards 9 and 8 and shortens its caption. Table 5's caption is shortened, Table 10's caption adds ArmoRM, and the author-block change causes local text reflow. Figures and empirical table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, empirical evidence, conclusions, and reproducibility appendix remain unchanged. Naming ArmoRM in Table 10 provides a small clarification, while Tables 1 and 5 become less self-contained but retain their explanations in the body. These local presentation tradeoffs do not produce a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
